correctness.rationale: The proof compares all unrestricted cyclic hosts with a flow on the full binary overlap graph. Each required-graph deficit source v must send one additional path to a target beginning 11; no path shorter than the index r(v) of the first 11 can do so. The bijection v=p11s -> 11s reverse(p) connects the source and a unique target with an allowed path of exactly r(v) steps. Balanced strong connectivity gives an Euler cycle. Counting p by Fibonacci numbers and s by Tribonacci avoidance yields the exact rational generating function. Recurrences and poles were recalculated; constructive Euler cycles k=3..16 and separate full-graph min-cost flows k=3..10 passed.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary literature contains the de Bruijn graph method, generic pattern-universal cycles and paired-graph hardness, but no formula for optimal covers of all binary words avoiding 111. The novel part assessed is the exact all-k Fibonacci–Tribonacci excess, the optimal reversed-prefix matching, and the unrestricted-host lower bound; generic Eulerian or directed postman reductions are prior knowledge. Searches cannot rule out unindexed equivalents.
residual_risks: Equivalent exact values or an identical reversed-prefix construction could be stated in unindexed or differently titled constrained de Bruijn or superstring literature.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial three-consecutive-ones binary shift has a natural optimal periodic k-window test problem. The result gives the exact all-window-length optimum even if forbidden words can be used as shortcuts; the optimal host nevertheless stays in the shift. The explicit path matching and positive limiting overhead (about 61.7 percent) characterize a genuine structural constraint, not a finite routine calculation.
